final_answer:
Let
\[
q=b^2+c,\qquad 
F=cw+cuv+bu^2+bv+au,
\]
and
\[
P=aX+(a^2+b)Y+(b^2+c)Z.
\]
I claim
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k\bigl[a,b,c,\;cw+cuv+bu^2+bv+au,\;aX+(a^2+b)Y+(b^2+c)Z\bigr]}.
\]

Write \(A=k[a,b,c,u,v,w]\). The relations say that \(R\) is the iterated differential-operator algebra over \(A\), with commuting operators \(X,Y,Z\), where
\[
[T,f]=\delta_T(f)\qquad (T=X,Y,Z,\ f\in A).
\]
Here \(\delta_X,\delta_Y,\delta_Z\) are the derivations determined by the displayed commutation relations.

First observe that \(a,b,c\) are central by hypothesis. Also direct substitution gives
\[
\delta_X(F)=\delta_Y(F)=\delta_Z(F)=0.
\]
For example,
\[
\delta_Z(F)
=b(a+2bu)+2bu(-b)+a(-b)
+c\bigl((-b)v+u(a+2bu)\bigr)+c(bv-au-2bu^2)=0,
\]
and the \(X,Y\) checks are the same cancellation. Hence \(F\) commutes with \(A,X,Y,Z\).

Next,
\[
a\delta_X+(a^2+b)\delta_Y+(b^2+c)\delta_Z=0
\]
on \(u,v,w\), and trivially on \(a,b,c\). Therefore
\[
[P,f]=0\qquad \forall f\in A.
\]
Since \(X,Y,Z\) commute with each other and with \(a,b,c\), we also have \([P,X]=[P,Y]=[P,Z]=0\). Thus
\[
k[a,b,c,F,P]\subseteq Z(R).
\]

It remains to prove there are no other central elements. Let \(K=k(a,b,c)\). After extending scalars to \(K\), set
\[
r=v+u^2.
\]
Then
\[
\delta_Z(u)=-b,\qquad \delta_Z(r)=a,
\]
and
\[
\delta_Y(u)=q,\qquad \delta_Y(r)=-ab.
\]
Also
\[
F=cw+cur+au+br.
\]
Over \(K\), the variables \(u,r,F\) are coordinates, and \(\delta_Y,\delta_Z\) act as two independent constant translations in the \((u,r)\)-plane while killing \(F\). Hence
\[
K[u,v,w]^{\delta_X,\delta_Y,\delta_Z}=K[F].
\]
Intersecting back with \(A\) gives
\[
A^{\delta_X,\delta_Y,\delta_Z}=k[a,b,c,F],
\]
because \(F\) is primitive over \(k[a,b,c]\).

Now take any central \(z\in R\). Filter \(R\) by total degree in \(X,Y,Z\). In the associated graded algebra
\[
\operatorname{gr}R=A[\xi,\eta,\zeta],
\]
the leading symbol \(\sigma(z)\) must commute, to top order, with every element of \(A\). Therefore its partial derivatives in \(\xi,\eta,\zeta\) give a syzygy among \(\delta_X,\delta_Y,\delta_Z\). The syzygy module is generated by
\[
(a,\ a^2+b,\ b^2+c),
\]
because solving
\[
\alpha\delta_X+\beta\delta_Y+\gamma\delta_Z=0
\]
on \(u,v\) gives
\[
\alpha=at,\qquad \beta=(a^2+b)t,\qquad \gamma=(b^2+c)t.
\]
Thus \(\sigma(z)\) depends on \(\xi,\eta,\zeta\) only through
\[
p=a\xi+(a^2+b)\eta+(b^2+c)\zeta.
\]
Centrality against \(X,Y,Z\) also forces its coefficients to lie in
\[
k[a,b,c,F].
\]
So
\[
\sigma(z)\in k[a,b,c,F,p].
\]
Subtracting the corresponding polynomial in \(P\) lowers the filtration degree. Induction on degree gives
\[
z\in k[a,b,c,F,P].
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k\bigl[a,b,c,\;cw+cuv+bu^2+bv+au,\;aX+(a^2+b)Y+(b^2+c)Z\bigr]}.
\]
